Memory for: How can I tell at a glance from the top of the editor whether I'm connected to the server and whether a sync is taking a while?
[1] Guide/Desktop Setup.md (Install and open a space)
  Protect and troubleshoot your space: Back up your local folder and test a restore into a separate folder. Sync can copy an unwanted edit or deletion to another device, so it does not replace a backup. / If another device is missing an edit, first check the Server sync status in the space’s settings and whether the Server is reachable. If the issue is inside the shared editor, start with [[Log]] and [[Troubleshooting]]. The browser cache reset instructions on that page apply to browser clients, not Desktop’s local files. / For shared configuration and libraries across Desktop spaces, see [[Meta Space]].
[2] Sync.md (Sync)
  Conflicts: When multiple clients change the same file around the same time, the server merges them automatically where it safely can. When it can’t (both sides touched the same words), it writes the file with a resolvable in-editor conflict, and you will be notified in the UI when this happens. See [[Collaboration]] for the full picture.
  SilverBullet is designed as an [[ADR/001 Offline-First PWA|Offline-First]] mindset — that is: your content should be available to you, whether you have an Internet connection or not. / Depending on the edition of SilverBullet that you use, Sync functions slightly differently. When you use the **Server** directly via the browser, your content will be synced to your browser’s local storage (IndexedDB). After an online load and initial sync, cached pages can be read and edited without a connection. Edits reconcile when the Server is reachable again. Documents have separate caching settings below. / [[Desktop]] spaces can _optionally_ be configured with [[Desktop Sync]]. / Regardless of the client, sync happens in near-real time when connected. Saves are throttled to about 2 seconds, after which the page is saved and synced immediately.
[3] Troubleshooting.md (Desktop)
  Desktop: For an error inside an open space, inspect the log in [[Workbench/Console]]. If it started after adding a script, style or library, review that change through the relevant Workbench tab. / If the local page is correct but another device has an older version, check the space’s **Sync** settings in the Desktop dashboard and confirm that the external Server is reachable. [[Desktop Sync]] explains the connection setup. If you do not use an external Server, there is no Desktop–Server sync to diagnose. / Check the dashboard’s **Updates** tab for an available update. For Flatpak installations, check through Flatpak instead. Before changing or replacing files to recover a space, preserve a copy. Desktop stores the space in a local folder. The browser cache reset below does not repair those files.

Exact facts:
- [1] Open the space and use [[Guide/My First Markdown Page]] to try the editor. [[Local Space]] explains the files Desktop keeps in the folder. Keep the folder’s location somewhere you can find when setting up backups.
- [1] If you want browser access or another Desktop installation to use the same content, you need a SilverBullet Server. You can [[Guide/Server Setup|run one yourself]] or use a hosting provider.
